hints.title: Subset State Representation
hints.text: Notice that the energy increment factor x depends solely on the number of locks that have already been broken.

hints.title: Ceiling Time Calculation
hints.text: For a lock with strength s and current rate x, the minutes required is (s + x - 1) // x.

hints.title: Bitmask Transitions
hints.text: Represent broken locks as bitmask of length n, transitioning to any remaining unbroken lock and taking the minimum total time.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Bitmask dynamic programming computes minimum minutes to break all locks across all permutations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all n! permutations sequentially is slower than memoized bitmask DP.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(2^n) states cached for fast lookup.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Observes that factor x depends only on the count of already broken locks, enabling bitmask DP.
